paper.title: Improved Regret Analysis for Variance-Adaptive Linear Bandits and Horizon-Free Linear Mixture MDPs

unmapped: Action set X_k is an arbitrary subset of the unit l2 ball, revealed each round (the paper does not say whether it may be chosen adaptively)
Rewards satisfy |r_k| <= 1/2 almost surely; noise is a martingale difference with unknown, time-varying conditional variance sigma_k^2
theta* lies in the unit l2 ball
settings.definition_quote: At time step $k$, the learner observes an arm set $\mathcal{X}_k \subseteq \mathbb{B}_2^d(1)$, chooses an arm $x_k \in \mathcal{X}_k$, pulls it. The learner then receives a stochastic reward $r_k = x_k^\T \th^*+\eps_k$ where $\th^* \in \mathbb{B}_2^d(1)$ ... $(i)$ $|r_k|\le [-1/2,1/2]$ almost surely, $(ii)$ $\mathbb{E}[\eps_k | \mathcal{F}_k]=0$ ..., and $(iii)$ $\mathbb{E}[\eps_k^2|\mathcal{F}_k]=\sigma_k^2$.

settings.name_in_paper: Linear mixture MDPs with unit cumulative rewards
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Episodic reinforcement learning (linear mixture MDP), not a bandit problem.
unmapped: Transition P = sum_i theta*_i P^i with known base models, theta* in the l1 unit ball
Total reward per episode lies in [0,1] (unit cumulative rewards); known reward function
Horizon-free: bound has no polynomial dependence on H
settings.definition_quote: The key modeling assumption of linear mixture MDPs is that the transition probability $P$ is a linear combination of a known set of models $\{P^i\}$, namely, $P=\sum_{i=1}^d \th_i^* P^i$ where $\th^* \in \mathbb{B}_1^d(1)$ ... Unit cumulative rewards: $\sum_{h=1}^H r_h^k \in [0,1]$ for any policy $\pi^k$.

source.label: main-thm-bandit
source.quote: VOFUL2 satisfies, with probability at least $1-2\dt$, \mathcal{R}^K =\tilde O\del{d^{1.5} \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^K \sig_k^2\ln(1/\dt)} + d^2 \ln(1/\dt)} where $\tilde O$ hides poly-logarithmic dependence on $\{d,K,\sum_{k=1}^K \sig_k^{2},  \ln(1/\dt)\}$.

results.notes: Holds with probability 1-2delta. Paper's K is the horizon T. Variances unknown to the learner. The conclusion says the algorithms are not computationally tractable, so compute is not polynomial as far as is known.

tuning: confidence set also includes the ell = 0 level

source.label: sec:dsqrtK
source.quote: Note that one can also show that VOFUL2 can be slightly modified to achieve the regret bound of $\tilde O\del[1]{  \min\cbr[1]{d\sqrt{K\ln(1/\dt)}, d^{1.5} \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^K \sig_k^2\ln(1/\dt)}} + d^2 \ln(1/\dt)} $, thus being no worse than OFUL.

results.notes: Not stated as a formal theorem: it is a claim in the main text, argued in Appendix sec:dsqrtK by reduction to the OFUL analysis. The exact failure probability is not stated.

conditions: unit cumulative rewards: sum_h r_h^k in [0,1]

source.label: main-rl
source.quote: With probability at least 1-$\dt$, \mathcal{R}^K =\sum_{k=1}^K [V^*(s_1^k)-V^k(s_1^k)] = \tilde O(d\sqrt{K\log^2(1/\dt)} + d^2\log (1/\dt))~. where $\tilde O$ hides poly-logarithmic dependence on $\{d,K,H, \ln(1/\dt)\}$.

results.notes: Horizon-free bound for linear mixture MDPs (out of scope: RL). Here d is the number of base models.
